item.title: India’s Exports to US Hold Firm After a Year of Trump’s Tariffs
item.description: India’s share of exports to the US remained largely unchanged despite a year of President Donald Trump’s punitive tariffs and New Delhi’s efforts to diversify its trade with a raft of new deals with other countries.

item.title: Chinese Cartoon So Bad You Have to See It Becomes Box Office Hit
item.description: A low-budget cartoon about a calf has become an unlikely box-office sensation in China, turning online ridicule into millions of dollars in ticket sales and sparking a debate over the merits of crude animation in the age of polished AI-generated entertainment.

item.title: Hong Kong Exchange Posts Record Earnings on IPO, Trading Boom
item.description: Hong Kong’s stock exchange beat market estimates with a 21% rise in second-quarter net income, fueled by robust trading volumes and a jump in initial public offerings.

item.title: Korean Won Advances Past Key Psychological Level of 1,400 Per Dollar
item.description: The South Korean won strengthened past the key psychological level of 1,400 per dollar for the first time in more than 10 months, extending a recovery fueled by a booming semiconductor industry.

item.title: CXMT Rival YMTC Moves Closer to China’s Next Marquee Chip IPO
item.description: Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. moved closer to an initial public offering in China, following in the footsteps of rival CXMT Corp.’s near-record share sale.

item.title: Chinese Coking Coal Futures Soar as Shanxi Supply Crunch Worsens
item.description: Chinese coking coal prices are surging as supply continues to tighten after the deadly accident in the mining hub of Shanxi three months ago.

item.title: FTSE Defers Indonesia Stock Additions to Indexes Until December
item.description: FTSE Russell will defer certain index changes for Indonesian equities until at least its December review, giving it more time to assess the effectiveness of market reforms by local authorities.

item.title: Ukraine's 150% Bond Market Rally Shows Traders It Can Beat the Odds
item.description: The four-year advance in Ukraine’s high-octane bond market is running strong.

item.title: Prize Worth £32 Billion if UK Tackles NHS Efficiency Crisis
item.description: The UK Treasury would be as much as £32 billion ($43.3 billion) better off each year if Britain’s government-run health service had kept pace with its pre-pandemic productivity gains, according to analysis of official figures.

item.title: Alphabet Set to Sell Long Aussie Bond at Record Near 7% Cost
item.description: Alphabet Inc. is poised to pay just under 7% to borrow longer-dated funds in its debut Australian dollar bond deal, in potentially its highest-ever coupon, underscoring how broader demands for cash among hyperscalers around the world are feeding into more costly funding almost everywhere.

item.title: India Stock Closing Auction Turmoil Clouds BSE’s Growth Outlook
item.description: A chaotic start to India’s bid to bring closing share-price discovery in line with global standards is hurting BSE Ltd., with some analysts questioning the growth outlook for Asia’s oldest exchange operator.

item.title: RBA’s Hauser Says Rates Will Need to Rise If Prices Fail to Ease
item.description: Australia’s central bank will need to raise interest rates again if upside risks to inflation are realized and consumer prices fail to come back down, Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said.

item.title: Funding $1 Trillion AI Capex May Expand Bond Supply, Robeco Says
item.description: A roughly $1 trillion wave of capital spending tied to artificial intelligence could add to bond supply and keep fixed-income markets volatile as hyperscalers race to fund infrastructure, according to the head of fixed income for Asia at Robeco.

item.title: Bain Unit Proterial Seeks $1.3 Billion From Japan Wire Firm Sale
item.description: Bain Capital subsidiary Proterial Ltd. is considering selling its wire, cable and automotive parts businesses, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: South Korea’s Household Loan Growth Jumps to Near Five-Year High
item.description: South Korea’s household loan growth jumped the most in nearly five years in the second quarter as home purchases and unsecured borrowing picked up, underscoring persistent financial-stability risks as the Bank of Korea considers further interest-rate hikes.

item.title: Copper Holds Loss as Deliveries to LME Mitigate Supply Crunch
item.description: Copper held the biggest loss in more than three weeks after traders made significant deliveries of the metal to London Metal Exchange warehouses, easing a historic squeeze.

item.title: South Korea Think Tank Raises Growth Outlook Above Government’s
item.description: South Korea’s state-run think tank raised its growth forecast for this year, surpassing the government’s already bullish projection as a stronger-than-expected global semiconductor boom, fueled by artificial intelligence, drives exports and investment.

item.title: WiseTech Raided by Australia Antitrust Watchdog; Stock Sinks
item.description: WiseTech Global Ltd. said Australian antitrust authorities demanded the company hand over documents and data as part of an investigation into alleged breaches of competition law. The company’s stock tumbled.

item.title: NSE Eyes $55 Billion Valuation in IPO While Rival BSE’s Shares Lose Favor
item.description: The IPO is expected to launch in the second half of September.

item.title: China Recovers Rocket on Land in Push to Catch Up With SpaceX
item.description: China said it recovered a rocket booster on land for the first time, a major step toward catching up with US firms like Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

item.title: Oasis Urges Kakaku.com to Withdraw Support for EQT’s Buyout Bid
item.description: Kakaku.com Inc. shareholder Oasis Management Co. has asked the company to withdraw its support for EQT AB’s buyout bid on grounds that the offer is too low, escalating a bidding war for the Japanese price comparison site.

item.title: Australia Wage Growth Stays Elevated, Reinforces Price Pressures
item.description: Australia’s wage growth remained elevated, highlighting persistent price pressures in the economy at a time when the Reserve Bank is warning it’s willing to tighten further to restrain inflation.

item.title: PHP/USD: Philippine Peso Fell to New Record Low as Oil Prices Rise
item.description: The Philippine peso fell to a record low against the dollar as higher oil prices put renewed pressure on the currency.

item.title: AI Startup Temporal in Talks for a Valuation of at Least $12 Billion
item.description: Temporal Technologies Inc. is in talks for a fresh funding round that would give the AI startup a valuation of at least $12 billion before the new money, according to people familiar with the efforts.

item.title: Japan Bond Volatility Is Pumping Up Futures Trading in Singapore
item.description: Global funds and relative-value traders are driving a surge in Japan bond futures trading in Singapore, drawn by rising volatility.

item.title: Hitachi Construction Shares Drop After $740 Million Block Trade
item.description: Hitachi Construction Machinery Co.’s shares fell the most in almost three weeks after its major shareholder Hitachi Ltd. offloaded all holding, in the latest move by the Japanese conglomerate to divest some of its assets to focus on core businesses.

item.title: Evergrande Liquidators Challenge Hong Kong Watchdog in Court
item.description: A Hong Kong court is set to hear arguments on whether a deal that set up a fund to compensate China Evergrande minority shareholders is valid.

item.title: Australian Housing Shares Surge as Earnings Defy Property Slump
item.description: Shares of two of Australia’s largest property developers surged after stronger full-year earnings showed resilience in the face of a housing market downturn.

item.title: Korean Stocks Bear Brunt of Chip Selloff on Higher Yield Worry
item.description: South Korea led a selloff in Asian chip stocks, as rising bond yields exacerbated worry over the large sums of cash being shelled out by Big Tech.

item.title: Japanese Stocks Slide as Bond Market Anxiety Hits AI Sentiment
item.description: Japan’s Nikkei Stock Average slumped for a second day, weighed down by chip-related stocks as anxiety over surging bond yields sapped risk appetite from the AI trade.
